name: [R12] Recursive resolver flooded with random-subdomain queries (DNS water torture)
message:
A high volume of NXDOMAIN-answered queries for distinct, pseudo-random subdomains under a single registered domain was observed at a recursive resolver. This is the classic 'DNS water torture' / random subdomain attack: forcing cache misses so every query is forwarded to the target domain's authoritative nameservers, exhausting their capacity. This is a volumetric availability signal, not proof of malicious intent by itself -- some CDN/anycast setups legitimately generate high-cardinality, often-missing subdomain traffic.

Tune: replace the allowlist with domains you expect legitimate high-cardinality subdomain traffic for; adjust the per-domain query-count and NXDOMAIN-ratio thresholds to your resolver's baseline.

cases.name: High-cardinality NXDOMAIN burst against one domain
